nt: Here, **the wind** represents one of the directions or sides of the world. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the side facing east]

Ezekiel is using the possessive form to describe a **reed** that was used for **measurement**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with the reed that he used for measuring]

The phrase **five cubits** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. There is, however, a correction that reads “500” in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [500 cubits]

Here, **to** marks **separate between the holy to common** as the goal or purpose of the **wall** that surrounded the temple area. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [its purpose was to separate between the holy and the common]

Ezekiel is using the adjectives **holy** and **common** as nouns. He could mean: (1) the **holy** area inside the wall and the **common** area outside the wall, Alternate translation: [the holy places to common places] or (2) any **holy** places, things, and people and any **common** places, things, and people. Alternate translation: [holy things to common things]
